paragraphs.source_en: You have been told also that life is darkness, and in your weariness you echo what was said by the weary.

units.source_en: You have been told also that life is darkness, and in your weariness you echo what was said by the weary.

paragraphs.source_en: And when you work with love you bind yourself to yourself, and to one another, and to God.

units.source_en: And when you work with love you bind yourself to yourself, and to one another, and to God.

paragraphs.source_en: It is to weave the cloth with threads drawn from your heart, even as if your beloved were to wear that cloth.

units.source_en: It is to weave the cloth with threads drawn from your heart, even as if your beloved were to wear that cloth.

ja.t: にまとうかのように、あなたの

paragraphs.source_en: It is to build a house with affection, even as if your beloved were to dwell in that house.

units.source_en: It is to build a house with affection, even as if your beloved were to dwell in that house.

paragraphs.source_en: It is to sow seeds with tenderness and reap the harvest with joy, even as if your beloved were to eat the fruit.

units.source_en: It is to sow seeds with tenderness and reap the harvest with joy, even as if your beloved were to eat the fruit.

ja.t: べるかのように、やさしさをもって

paragraphs.source_en: Often have I heard you say, as if speaking in sleep, “He who works in marble, and finds the shape of his own soul in the stone, is nobler than he who ploughs the soil. And he who seizes the rainbow to lay it on a cloth in the likeness of man, is more than he who makes the sandals for our feet.”

units.source_en: And he who seizes the rainbow to lay it on a cloth in the likeness of man, is more than he who makes the sandals for our feet.”

paragraphs.source_en: But I say, not in sleep but in the overwakefulness of noontide, that the wind speaks not more sweetly to the giant oaks than to the least of all the blades of grass;

units.source_en: But I say, not in sleep but in the overwakefulness of noontide, that the wind speaks not more sweetly to the giant oaks than to the least of all the blades of grass;

ja.t: りかけるときも、いちばん

paragraphs.source_en: And he alone is great who turns the voice of the wind into a song made sweeter by his own loving.

units.source_en: And he alone is great who turns the voice of the wind into a song made sweeter by his own loving.

paragraphs.source_en: And if you cannot work with love but only with distaste, it is better that you should leave your work and sit at the gate of the temple and take alms of those who work with joy.

units.source_en: And if you cannot work with love but only with distaste, it is better that you should leave your work and sit at the gate of the temple and take alms of those who work with joy.

paragraphs.source_en: For if you bake bread with indifference, you bake a bitter bread that feeds but half man’s hunger.

units.source_en: For if you bake bread with indifference, you bake a bitter bread that feeds but half man’s hunger.

paragraphs.source_en: And if you grudge the crushing of the grapes, your grudge distils a poison in the wine. And if you sing though as angels, and love not the singing, you muffle man’s ears to the voices of the day and the voices of the night.

paragraphs.source_en: And the selfsame well from which your laughter rises was oftentimes filled with your tears.

paragraphs.source_en: Is not the cup that holds your wine the very cup that was burned in the potter’s oven?
